pairs.reason: Same comparative claim (mind over tool/artifact), only rephrased.
'Fixed course of development' carries the same contrast as 'inevitable process'; collective choice is kept.
'Even if policy stays as it is' keeps the same no-policy-change condition.
'Claims about what AI will achieve' matches 'promises', and 'overstated' matches 'inflated hype' without the loaded word.
'Strong enough in themselves to win out' matches 'enough inherent force to prevail'.

The original rejects treating humans as any stage to surpass, which includes transhumanist self-enhancement; the rewrite rejects only AI creating successor beings, so an enhancement advocate could disagree with the original but agree with the rewrite.
pairs.fix: AI should serve human beings as its end, and humanity should not be treated as a stage to be surpassed.

pairs.reason: Same contrast and the same present time frame.
'Good guide' sets a higher bar than 'valid guide': someone who thinks history is a legitimate but rough reference class agrees with the original but may reject the rewrite.
pairs.fix: The history of earlier general-purpose technologies is a valid guide to how AI will behave and how people will receive it.

pairs.reason: 'Should by default outweigh one's own reasoning' keeps the default-deference claim; the change in wording is minor.
'Unelected bodies' is narrower than 'unelected powers': it can leave out rule by corporations or AI systems, which matters on an AI quiz.
pairs.fix: Political authority should rest on popular self-government rather than on experts, executives or other unelected powers.

pairs.reason: 'Good for people on balance' matches 'serves human beings on balance'.
Same threshold, the same time frame and the same causal mechanism.
'Not directed or controlled by the state' matches 'separate from state direction and control'; dropping 'remain' removes only a presupposition.
Same contrast; 'technological singularity' resolves the intended sense of 'singularity' without changing the scope.

new.problems: 'Safe' has no stated standard (fully safe, or safe enough to deploy?), so people may answer different questions; the claim is otherwise plainly phrased.
'Sufficiently powerful' leaves the threshold open, so the statement is close to true by definition and both camps may agree while picturing different thresholds.
